variants.title: Exoplanet transit light curve (SIMULATED DATA, Kepler-like)
variants.sample: SIMULATED Kepler-like target: faint star, 29.4-minute cadence, 88 days
variants.method: box least-squares period search and folded light curve
variants.unknown: the planet radius ratio, the orbital period and the inclination
variants.note: SIMULATED DATA, not an observation of any real star. A Neptune-sized planet around a Sun-like star: a shallower dip, a longer period and a lower noise per point at the long cadence of the Kepler mission.

source.title: Borucki et al. (2010), Science 327, 977: Kepler long cadence 29.4 minutes (the cadence only; the star and planet are invented)

variants.aim: Analyse a SIMULATED Kepler-like light curve (29.4-minute cadence, 88 days): find the period by box least squares, fold, measure depth and duration, and deduce the radius ratio and inclination of an invented Neptune-sized planet.
